title: Haze pushes Singapore’s air quality into the unhealthy range on Saturday
dek: The 24-hour PSI ranged from 118 in the south to 148 in the west on Saturday morning, with smoke from fires in Sumatra still drifting over the island.
body: Singapore woke to hazy skies on Saturday as the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index climbed into the unhealthy range across much of the island, from 118 in the south to 148 in the west. Hourly PM2.5 levels were elevated everywhere, with the west recording the highest reading.

The National Environment Agency said smoke from fires in Sumatra can keep reaching Singapore while winds blow from the south. It forecast a national 24-hour PSI of between 90 and 140 for the day and advised people to check hourly PM2.5 readings before any long or strenuous activity outdoors.

Some relief may be on the way. Thundery showers are expected over northern, eastern and central areas in the afternoon, and winds are forecast to turn to the south-west or west from Sunday, which should carry less smoke towards Singapore.

title: Indonesia cuts natural gas exports to Singapore from today
dek: Supplies from Natuna and Sumatra will fall by a combined 31 billion British thermal units a day as Jakarta puts domestic demand first.
body: Indonesia has started reducing the natural gas it pipes to Singapore, cutting supplies by 31 billion British thermal units a day: 15 from the Natuna fields and 16 from pipelines in Sumatra. The head of the upstream oil and gas regulator, SKK Migas, announced the cut in Jakarta on Friday.

The cut affects only Singapore, because those export pipelines run directly to the island. Indonesia’s energy minister said the country must meet its own needs first and suggested it may not extend gas export deals with neighbours when they expire.

About 40 per cent of Singapore’s natural gas arrives by pipeline from Indonesia and Malaysia, with the rest shipped in as liquefied natural gas from around the world. Singapore’s existing import contracts with Indonesia run until the end of 2028.

title: Typhoon Champi shuts down Taiwan as nearly 1,000 flights are cancelled
dek: Schools, offices and financial markets closed across most of the island. One person has died and 94 were injured as the storm skirted the north-east coast.
body: Almost all of Taiwan closed on Friday as Typhoon Champi, at one point a super typhoon, passed off the island’s north-east coast with gusts of around 190 km/h near its centre. All 262 domestic flights and 717 international flights were cancelled, and financial markets did not open.

One person was killed and 94 were injured, and nearly 1,300 people were moved out of mountainous areas. High-speed rail kept running and Taipei’s metro operated a reduced service. Only the Kinmen islands kept schools and offices open as normal.

Forecasters expect the storm to turn north towards the Chinese coast and then into southern Japan, passing near Yonaguni in Okinawa first. Taiwan’s weather agency warned that landfall could not be ruled out if the typhoon stalls.

title: Magnitude 7.0 earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16 people
dek: The quake struck a remote area of Nagqu late on Thursday. Rescuers are working at altitude on blocked roads, with snow forecast.
body: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck the Nagqu area of Tibet at 10.33pm on Thursday, killing at least 16 people and injuring dozens, according to Chinese state media and local officials. The epicentre was in mountainous terrain about 390 km north-east of Lhasa.

Officials reported that 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, and power and phone lines were cut. China activated a level-two emergency response, and around 1,600 rescue workers were sent to an area that sits at roughly 4,800 metres above sea level.
Rescuers face rockfalls and blocked roads, and snow is forecast in the coming days. Officials warned that the number of casualties could still rise as teams reach more remote villages.

title: Iran says seven tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz and warns US bases
dek: The Revolutionary Guards say four tankers caught fire and three struck mines. The US says the shipping lanes are clear and most vessels are getting through.
body: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that seven oil tankers had been struck in the Strait of Hormuz overnight. Four were hit while transferring oil and caught fire, and three were disabled by mines, the Guards said. The claims could not be independently verified, and no casualties were reported.

If confirmed, it would be the largest single-day toll in the waterway since the war began in February. The Guards warned that the conflict could spread to US bases in the region if Washington helps tankers through other parts of the strait.

US Central Command disputed the claims, saying the international shipping lanes had been cleared and about 95 per cent of vessels were getting through. President Donald Trump accused Iran of trying to push up oil prices before the US midterm elections.

title: Almost all of the world’s coral reef systems are critically endangered, IUCN warns
dek: A new global assessment rates 96% of reef systems at the highest risk level, including the Coral Triangle and the Great Barrier Reef.
body: The International Union for Conservation of Nature has classified 96 per cent of the planet’s coral reef systems as critically endangered, its highest risk category. The assessment covered 127 tropical and subtropical reef systems spanning more than 188,000 square kilometres.

The study found that almost all shallow-water reefs face a very high risk of collapse within 50 years, driven mainly by warming seas and more frequent bleaching. Reefs rated critically endangered include the Coral Triangle around Southeast Asia, the Great Barrier Reef and the Red Sea.

Researchers said most reefs are not yet lost and that resilient pockets can survive if they are protected. Reefs support about a quarter of marine species and matter for fisheries, tourism and coastal protection across the region.
